lines.text: Pietra dura is Italian for hard stones.
lines.say: PYEH-trah DOO-rah is Italian for hard stones.

lines.text: It is a Florentine art of joining thin slices of colored stone.
Each slice is cut to shape and joined edge to edge.
The joins are filed so smooth that the seams barely show.
Craftsmen used stones such as lapis lazuli and jasper.
Rome revived stone inlay in the 1500s, and Florence became a rival.

post.caption: Pietra dura is Italian for hard stones. It is a Florentine art of joining thin slices of colored stone. Each slice is cut to shape and joined edge to edge. The joins are filed so smooth that the seams barely show. Craftsmen used stones such as lapis lazuli and jasper. Rome revived stone inlay in the 1500s, and Florence became a rival. In 1588 Grand Duke Ferdinando de' Medici founded the workshop. It started inside the Uffizi as the Galleria dei Lavori. Florentine pietra dura brooches were popular tourist souvenirs. Today the Opificio delle Pietre Dure restores art in Florence.
